text: In an ApoE4 astrocyte model, pharmacologically targeting the CREB pathway to raise NHE6 expression regulated endosomal pH and restored defective amyloid-beta clearance. This implies an endosomal pH defect in ApoE4 astrocytes that NHE6 upregulation can correct, but the abstract reports no APOE4 vs APOE3 pH comparison. Class 5 because A (APOE genotype) is not the variable perturbed in the reported comparison; the perturbation is a drug acting on the CREB/NHE6 pathway.
description: ApoE4 astrocyte model (species, cell source and comparator unspecified in the abstract), treated with pharmacological modulators of the CREB pathway; endosomal pH and Abeta clearance assays. Abstract only; full text unavailable. Caveat: no APOE3 comparison is stated, the direction of the pH change is not stated, and the cells may not be human or non-AD.

provenance.excerpt: Control of NHE6 expression by pharmacological targeting of the CREB pathway can be used to regulate endosomal pH and restore defective amyloid Aβ clearance in an ApoE4 astrocyte model of Alzheimer’s disease.

meccogFinding.summary: (CREB pathway drug -> increased NHE6 in ApoE4 astrocytes) -> (altered endosomal pH; restored Abeta clearance) [implies APOE4 endosomal pH defect correctable by NHE6]
